# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 37 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 37-38 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_037_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 37

**1** His disciples said: "When will you be revealed to us and when will we see you?"

**2** Jesus said: "When you strip [вст] without being ashamed [шіпе] and take your garments [швшт] and place them under your feet like little children [шнре коуі] and trample [пате] on them,

**3** then you will see the Son of the Living One [шнре нпетоноз] and you will not be afraid."

---

**Textual Notes (EMET):**
- *вст*: to undress, strip naked
- *шіпе*: shame, embarrassment; "without shame" = shamelessness of the pre-fallen state
- *швшт*: garments, clothing; the socially constructed self
- *пате*: to trample, tread upon
- *шнре нпетоноз*: "Son of the Living One" — a key Christological title in Thomas
- The disciples ask about the Parousia (when will we see you?); Jesus answers with an anti-shame nakedness ritual
- The stripping and trampling of garments = divesting of the social/bodily self
- cf. Saying 21 (the children strip their clothes) — the image recurs
- The "Son of the Living One" = the divine image; the vision is of Jesus but also of the divine self
